query: Explain how to compare two home air-quality interventions for particulate matter, including evidence quality, measurement design, and important limitations.

requirements.text: Describe a credible particulate-matter measurement design

candidates.title: Portable filtration
candidates.content: A correctly sized particle filter can reduce indoor particulate concentrations while operating. Performance depends on clean-air delivery rate, room volume, placement, fan setting, filter loading, and outdoor infiltration. The document is synthetic and was authored only for development-set harness testing; it is not scored benchmark evidence.

candidates.title: Source control
candidates.content: Removing indoor emission sources and reducing particle entry can prevent pollution rather than treating it after release. Effects vary with cooking, smoking, ventilation behavior, building leakage, and outdoor conditions. The document is synthetic and was authored only for development-set harness testing; it is not scored benchmark evidence.

candidates.title: Measurement design
candidates.content: Use calibrated sensors in comparable locations, establish a baseline, record intervention periods, and track outdoor particulate matter, occupancy, ventilation, and episodic sources. Repeated measurements are stronger than one before-after reading. The document is synthetic and was authored only for development-set harness testing; it is not scored benchmark evidence.

candidates.title: Evidence limits
candidates.content: Sensor error, temporal confounding, room differences, adherence, and short follow-up can exaggerate an apparent effect. Lower particle concentration is an intermediate outcome and does not by itself prove a health benefit. The document is synthetic and was authored only for development-set harness testing; it is not scored benchmark evidence.
